In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MPT was a gradual process, with the most prominent change being a strengthening of the glacial–inter glacial contrast in the regional conveyor circulation after 650 ka.

the MPT was not only characterised by an increase in glacial–inter-glacial amplitudes, but also by an increase of the frequency of glacial–inter- glacial transitions and by an increase in the complexity of climate responses.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the MPT is a gradual transition in which changes in climate, productivity and regional conveyor circulation are not in phase with each other and do not occur in perfect synchronicity with the global 100–kyr cycle.
the onset of the 100-kyrs cycles is not only a global phenomenon but that the regional response to these cycles also started earlier than previously assumed.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the MPT was not an instantaneous event.

the MPT was a gradual process, with the most important climate changes occurring in the interval from 1 to 0.8 Myr, and that the MPT in the southeastern Atlantic is not a simple reflection of the 100-kyrs glacial–intergalacials cycles.
